NovaBio Therapeutics - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Therapeutics Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Therapeutics' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Emily Carter, Chief Executive Officer; Johnathan Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Lisa Wong, Chief Scientific Officer; Tom Bradley, Head of Commercial; Karen Lee, Head of Manufacturing; and Robert Singh, Head of Regulatory Affairs.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Carter, CEO of NovaBio Therapeutics.

Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBio Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the second quarter, driven by robust demand for our flagship oncology assets like OncoTarget-7 and key regulatory milestones that expanded our addressable markets. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including pipeline advancement, global expansion, and portfolio optimization.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, focusing on our overall performance highlights and key takeaways, product revenue by key drug franchise with volume and price analysis, regulatory approvals and label expansions achieved, operating expense analysis, business development including licensing deals acquisitions and partnerships, marketing and sales effectiveness metrics, patent cliff exposure and life cycle management strategies, and cash flow and balance sheet highlights.

We are particularly excited about GeneXpert RA, our CRISPR-based gene editing therapy for rheumatoid arthritis, and its potential to transform treatment paradigms in autoimmune diseases with durable, one-time interventions.

Now, I will turn the call over to Johnathan Hale, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Johnathan Hale, CFO:
Thank you, Emily. As Emily mentioned, we had a solid second quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $875 million, an increase of 28% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong volume growth in our oncology franchise and contributions from new launches like GeneXpert RA.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $210 million, or $1.85 per share. Non-GAAP net income was a stronger $245 million, or $2.15 per share.

Our operating expenses were $452 million, reflecting disciplined investments in R&D and efficiencies in SG&A. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to support our pipeline. Our cash position remains strong at $4.2 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to $3.45 to $3.55 billion in revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $8.40 to $8.60.

To give you a fuller picture, let me walk through our overall performance highlights and key takeaways for Q2 2024, which underscore NovaBio Therapeutics' continued momentum in the oncology and rare disease landscapes. We delivered another exceptional quarter, exceeding our guidance across key metrics and reinforcing our position as a leader in next-generation targeted therapies.

Starting with the top line: total revenue reached $875 million, up 28% year-over-year and 5% above the midpoint of our guidance range. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, driven primarily by robust demand for our flagship asset, OncoTarget-7, our bispecific T-cell engager for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, which generated $520 million in net product sales—a 35% YoY increase. Volume growth accounted for 22 points of that uplift, fueled by expanded label indications in frontline settings following our successful sNDA approval in March, while pricing held firm at an ASP of $185,000 per treatment course despite ongoing payer negotiations. Our newer launch, GeneXpert RA, contributed $120 million in its first full quarter post-launch, hitting 110% of our internal ramp expectations thanks to strong formulary wins with CVS Caremark and Express Scripts.

Geographically, U.S. revenues grew 32% to $580 million, representing 66% of the total, bolstered by our J-code reimbursement for OncoTarget-7 and penetration into community oncology settings via our expanded partnership with Cardinal Health. In Europe, sales rose 22% to $195 million, or 22% of total revenue, with uptake in Germany and the UK offsetting some biosimilar erosion on our legacy immunology portfolio—think Humira-like pressures, but we've mitigated this through our switch to premium next-gen assets. Emerging markets, now 12% of revenue at $105 million, surged 45% YoY, led by our out-licensing deal with Sun Pharma in India for OncoTarget-7 generics post-patent expiry in 2028, and initial launches in Brazil via our ANMAT approval.

On the profitability front, we reported GAAP net income of $210 million, or $1.85 diluted EPS, versus $1.42 last year—a 30% improvement. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $2.15, beating consensus by $0.12. Gross margins expanded 420 basis points to 89.2%, reflecting manufacturing efficiencies at our Singapore facility, where we've scaled viral vector production for GeneXpert RA by 150% using single-use bioreactors. R&D expenses rose 15% to $220 million, or 25% of revenue—still below the industry average of 28% for large-cap biotechs—supporting a robust pipeline with five Phase 3 readouts expected by year-end, including the pivotal ORION-3 trial for OncoTarget-7 in solid tumors. SG&A was disciplined at 18% of revenue, down from 20% last year, as we leveraged digital sales enablement tools akin to Veeva Systems' CRM platform to optimize our 1,200-person field force.

Operationally, free cash flow generation was stellar at $320 million, bolstering our cash position to $4.2 billion with net debt at just 0.8x EBITDA. This liquidity gives us ample dry powder for bolt-on M&A—we've already closed the $1.1 billion acquisition of Helix Oncology in May, adding two early-stage ADCs with best-in-class payloads similar to Enhertu's DXd technology.

Key trends shaping our performance include the ongoing shift toward precision medicine, where our companion diagnostics for OncoTarget-7—partnered with Foundation Medicine—now cover 75% of eligible patients, driving adherence rates above 92%. We're also capitalizing on the IRA's impact; while small-molecule pricing caps pose headwinds, our biologics portfolio remains largely exempt, and we've proactively layered in value-based agreements with 60% of Medicare Part D plans. Biosimilar competition intensified, with uptake on our adalimumab biosimilar reaching 45% share, but this was more than offset by 18% growth in our novel modalities.

Strategically, we're accelerating three pillars: first, pipeline derisking via AI-driven target identification—our proprietary NovaAI platform, trained on 50 petabytes of multimodal data, has cut hit-to-lead timelines by 40%, mirroring Exscientia's model but scaled for internal use. Second, global expansion, with a new $500 million fill-finish plant in Ireland breaking ground next month to support EU launches and mitigate U.S. capacity constraints. Third, portfolio optimization, including a $300 million share repurchase authorization announced today, signaling confidence in our 15-20% CAGR through 2027.

In summary, Q2 validates our thesis: disciplined execution in a high-barrier industry yields outsized returns. We're raising full-year guidance to $3.45-$3.55 billion in revenue—up 6% at the midpoint—and non-GAAP EPS to $8.40-$8.60, implying 22% growth. Looking ahead, with 70% of our revenue from products launched post-2020 and a Phase 3 pipeline valued at over $15 billion in peak sales potential, NovaBio is primed to deliver sustained value creation amid favorable tailwinds like the $100 billion+ U.S. oncology market expansion.

Now, turning to a deeper dive on product revenue by key drug franchise with volume and price analysis. Overall, net product sales reached $1.45 billion in the quarter, up 28% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter, driven by robust volume growth across the board, partially offset by targeted pricing actions in response to payer dynamics. Ex-manufacturing, this represents our strongest top-line quarter to date, underscoring the durability of our innovative portfolio amid a challenging macro environment with persistent inflation and biosimilar erosion in legacy categories.

Let me break this down by franchise, incorporating volume and ASP analysis based on IQVIA NPA and Xponent data, as well as our internal patient and script metrics. I'll highlight YOY and sequential trends, regional nuances, and the technical and strategic levers we're pulling.

Our Oncology franchise: $785 million, +35% YOY, +15% QOQ. This remains our growth engine, now representing 54% of total product sales—up from 48% a year ago. Flagship asset OncoNova (our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibody, akin to the Keytruda/Opdivo class) drove the lion's share at $620 million, up 42% YOY. Volume: TRx grew 38% YOY to 145,000 scripts, with NRx up 45%, capturing 18% U.S. market share in 1L NSCLC—a 300 bps expansion—thanks to our recent sBLA approval for frontline combo with our next-gen ADC, NovaTox. Patient days on therapy increased 22% to 4.2 million, reflecting improved adherence from our digital patient support platform, which now engages 65% of eligible patients. Ex-U.S., volumes surged 55% in China via our partnership with Sinopharm, where we're ramping post-NMPA approval. ASP: Flat YOY at ~$145,000 per patient-year, but down 2% sequentially due to ~$50 million in U.S. gross-to-net adjustments from 340B carve-outs and higher Medicare rebates under the Inflation Reduction Act. In Europe, ASP held steady at €120,000 amid EMA pricing stability. Sequentially, label expansion into MSI-high solid tumors added ~10,000 new patients, while we're mitigating biosimilar risks to our earlier EGFR inhibitor through a lifecycle management strategy, including a Phase 3 readout expected Q4 for a subcutaneous formulation to boost convenience and retention.

Immunology Franchise: $410 million, +22% YOY, +8% QOQ. Immunology contributed 28% of sales, with ImmunoBlock (our IL-23/IL-17 dual inhibitor for plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis, comparable to Tremfya or Bimzelx) at $380 million, up 25% YOY. Volume: U.S. TRx rose 28% to 220,000, with market share steady at 22% per IQVIA, fueled by a 15% share gain in bio-naïve patients following our head-to-head superiority data vs. Skyrizi at AAD 2024. Globally, volumes grew 20%, with Europe up 30% post-reimbursement in Germany and France, and Emerging Markets (ex-China) adding 12% from Brazil and India launches. Patient persistence hit 78% at 12 months, up from 72% YOY, driven by our co-pay assistance program capping out-of-pocket at $5/month for 90% of commercial lives. ASP: Up 1% YOY to $52,000 per patient-year, reflecting favorable EU tender wins, but sequential pressure of -3% from U.S. PBM rebating escalation—now at 45% of gross sales. We're countering this with value-based contracting pilots, tying ~20% of U.S. rebates to 24-month persistence outcomes. Strategic insight: With patent expiry looming in 2028, we're accelerating our bispecific pipeline, including ImmunoNext (IL-4/13 + TSLP), with Phase 3 topline due H1 2025, positioning us to defend $2B+ peak sales potential.

Rare Diseases & Gene Therapies Franchise: $255 million, +15% YOY, +10% QOQ. This high-margin franchise, 18% of sales, is ramping post our 2023 gene therapy approvals. Lead GeneFix (AAV-based therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, similar to Elevidys) delivered $210 million. Volume: U.S. infusions grew 25% to 1,200 patients, with NRx up 40% after FDA expansion to ambulatory DMD patients aged 4+. Europe added 150 treatments via conditional EMA approval, while Japan volumes doubled through our Chugai alliance. Utilization of our single-dose model remains strong, with 95% one-time administration compliance. ASP: +5% YOY to $1.85 million per treatment—premium pricing justified by 2.5-year event-free survival data from our long-term extension study—but -1% sequentially from Medicaid clawbacks. Ex-U.S. ASP at $1.6 million reflects harmonized global pricing strategy. Key initiative: We're scaling manufacturing with a new 50,000 L bioreactor at our North Carolina facility, targeting 2x capacity by year-end to support pipeline readouts in Pompe and Fabry diseases. This franchise boasts 85% gross margins, providing downside protection.

Regional commentary: U.S. (72% of sales): $1.04B, +30% YOY; volume-led, tempered by 48% gross-to-net. Europe (15%): $220M, +25% YOY; strong tenders offsetting HTA headwinds. Ex-US/China/EM (13%): $190M, +35% YOY; China Oncology up 60% on reimbursement inclusion in NRDL.

Forward outlook: We're raising full-year net product sales guidance to $5.6-5.8B, implying 26-30% growth, with Oncology pacing at 35%+. Risks include IRA price caps on select small molecules starting 2026, which we're addressing via innovation—$2.5B R&D investment yielding 12 Phase 3 assets—and bolt-on M&A, like our recent $800M acquisition of a PROTAC degrader platform. This positions NovaBio for sustained 20%+ CAGR through the decade, outpacing peers amid patent cliffs at the likes of AbbVie and J&J.

Next, our operating expense analysis for the second quarter, where we continue to demonstrate disciplined capital allocation amid a dynamic biotech landscape. Total operating expenses for Q2 came in at $452 million, up 12% year-over-year from $404 million in Q2 2023, but flat sequentially from Q1 2024 on an adjusted basis. As a percentage of our trailing twelve-month revenue, OPEX stood at 78%, an improvement from 85% a year ago, reflecting the early revenue ramp from our lead oncology asset, NovaCelsis – our PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, which launched in the U.S. in late 2023 and is mirroring uptake patterns seen with Merck's Keytruda in metastatic NSCLC indications.

Breaking it down by major line items, starting with our core investment area: R&D, which accounted for $325 million, or 72% of total OPEX – up 18% YoY but down 2% sequentially as we lap elevated preclinical spend from last year. This increase was driven by three key Phase 3 readouts expected in H2: BNT-401, our next-gen CAR-T for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, advancing in the U.S. and EU with FDA Fast Track and EMA PRIME designations; our CRISPR-based gene editing candidate, NovaEdit-23, for sickle cell disease, where we've dosed over 150 patients across U.S. and U.K. sites; and the global pivotal trial for our mRNA-lipid nanoparticle platform targeting Alzheimer's, in partnership with a top-tier CRO like IQVIA. Regionally, U.S. R&D spend represented 55% of the total at $179 million, fueled by high-cost domestic clinical operations and manufacturing scale-up at our North Carolina facility to support CMC requirements under the FDA's accelerated approval pathway. Europe contributed 25% or $81 million, primarily milestone payments to our alliance with AstraZeneca on the Alzheimer's program, offset by grant funding from the Innovative Medicines Initiative. Asia-Pacific, at 15% or $49 million, saw efficiencies from our Shanghai outpost partnering with WuXi Biologics for low-cost process development, reducing per-patient trial costs by 22% YoY.

Strategically, we're leveraging AI-driven initiatives to optimize R&D productivity – our proprietary AlphaFold-integrated platform has cut hit-to-lead timelines by 35% for small-molecule kinase inhibitors, similar to Recursion Pharmaceuticals' approach, allowing us to advance five new INDs into preclinical this quarter without proportional headcount growth. We reduced our R&D burn rate per pipeline asset to $28 million from $34 million YoY through targeted outsourcing, maintaining a robust 18-month cash runway post our recent $750 million convertible notes offering.

Moving to SG&A, which totaled $115 million, up just 4% YoY and 1% sequentially – a testament to our lean commercialization model. This category broke out as 48% sales and marketing ($55 million), 32% general and administrative ($37 million), and 20% other ($23 million, including restructuring credits). Sales and marketing ramped modestly to support NovaCelsis' U.S. launch, where we've deployed a 220-person specialty sales force targeting key accounts in community oncology centers – achieving 65% market access with payers like CVS Caremark and mirroring the disciplined build-out Bristol Myers Squibb used for Opdivo. YoY growth was tempered by 12% lower medical affairs spend as KOL engagements shifted virtual post-launch. G&A efficiencies stemmed from a 7% headcount reduction in non-core functions via our 2023 reorganization, saving $15 million annualized, while investing in digital transformation – ERP migration to SAP S/4HANA to streamline royalty tracking from our out-licensed JAK inhibitor to Incyte. Regionally, U.S. SG&A was 70% of the total, with Europe at 20% focused on pricing/reimbursement negotiations for NovaCelsis under the EMA's ATMP classification, and APAC at 10% supporting our ex-U.S. early access programs in China via the NMPA's breakthrough therapy designation.

Other notable trends: Manufacturing and supply chain costs within OPEX fell 8% YoY to $12 million, thanks to tech transfer efficiencies at our Singapore CDMO partner, Lonza, amid softening API pricing pressures from Indian generics. We also booked a $5 million restructuring credit from facility consolidations, aligning with industry peers like Amgen in optimizing post-COVID capacity.

Looking forward, we guide full-year 2024 OPEX to $1.85 billion to $1.95 billion, implying 10-13% YoY growth, with R&D at 70-72% of the mix. This embeds $150 million in incremental pipeline investments, offset by $80 million in productivity gains from AI/ML in trial design and real-world evidence analytics via our Veeva Vault integration. In a market where peers like Regeneron are facing 20%+ R&D inflation from inflation and talent competition, our 5% structural OPEX-to-revenue deleveraging positions us for sustained mid-teens EBITDA margins by 2026, assuming two Phase 3 successes and NovaCelsis peak sales of $2.5 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Johnathan. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, our oncology pipeline advanced with positive topline data from the ORION-3 Phase 3 trial for OncoTarget-7 in solid tumors, demonstrating a 42% improvement in progression-free survival. In rare diseases, the GENESIS trial for GenHeal in spinal muscular atrophy Type 1 met all primary endpoints with 92% event-free survival. We're also advancing NovaEdit-23 in sickle cell disease, with over 150 patients dosed. We expect to report five Phase 3 readouts by year-end, including BNT-401 CAR-T and our Alzheimer's mRNA program.

Next, Dr. Lisa Wong will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Lisa Wong, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Michael. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Our NovaAI platform has accelerated hit-to-lead timelines by 40%, enabling five new INDs this quarter. We're advancing bispecific antibodies, PROTAC degraders, and CRISPR gene editing candidates, with preclinical data supporting combos like PD-1 with next-gen ADCs. Our AlphaFold-integrated tools have reduced failure rates, positioning us for 12 Phase 3 assets.

Now I'll turn the call over to Tom Bradley, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Tom Bradley, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Lisa. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with net product sales up 28% driven by oncology leadership. We are seeing strong uptake in OncoTarget-X in NSCLC and GeneFix in rare genetic disorders. Our marketing campaigns are proving effective, with return on marketing investment at 4.8x.

Diving deeper into our marketing and sales effectiveness metrics for Q2, which continue to demonstrate robust execution across our portfolio. Sales effectiveness isn't just about top-line revenue—it's about optimizing reach, frequency, and conversion in a highly regulated environment amid intensifying competition from biosimilars and next-gen therapies like Merck's Keytruda expansions and Regeneron's Dupixent analogs.

Our overall return on marketing investment—or ROMI—stood at 4.8x for the quarter, up from 4.2x YoY, driven by a 12% uplift in new-to-brand prescription (NRx) growth to 18% quarter-over-quarter. Total Rx volume for OncoTarget-X hit 285,000 scripts, capturing 22% segment share in first-line NSCLC, per IQVIA data, while GeneFix maintained 65% share in its ultra-orphan market despite payer pushback on gene therapy pricing.

Sales Force Effectiveness (SFE): Our field team of 1,250 representatives—optimized through our 2023 realignment post-OncoTarget-X label expansion—delivered industry-leading productivity. Average daily HCP touches reached 8.2, a 15% increase from Q2 '23, with reach and frequency metrics at 78% of core high-decile prescribers monthly—well above the 65% peer average from Veeva benchmarks. Share of voice in oncology held steady at 26%, outpacing Roche's Tecentriq at 19% in key US markets, thanks to our targeted detailing on PD-L1 high expressors.

Regionally, US performance was stellar: Northeast and Southeast territories saw 22% NRx uplift, fueled by 92% formulary coverage on CVS Caremark and Express Scripts PBM lists after our value-based contracting wins. In Europe, post-EMA approval for OncoTarget-X combo with chemo, we achieved 68% reach among EU5 KOLs, driving 14% TRx growth despite HTA headwinds in Germany and France—our NICE submission for GeneFix also secured reimbursed status at £450K per treatment, aligning with peers like Bluebird Bio's Zynteglo. Asia-Pacific lagged slightly at 9% NRx growth due to Japan PMDA delays, but our 45-rep team there boosted share of voice to 18% via partnerships with Takeda, offsetting local generics. Emerging markets, now 8% of sales, grew 25% YoY with low-cost digital pilots in Brazil and India.

Digital and Omnichannel Initiatives: We've leaned heavily into tech to amplify traditional SFE. Our AI-powered NextBestAction platform, integrated with Veeva CRM and powered by Salesforce Einstein, increased HCP engagement conversion by 28%—recommending personalized content like our VR simulation for OncoTarget-X's IO mechanism, viewed by 42,000 oncologists YTD. Omnichannel metrics show 65% of interactions now hybrid: 55% digital (webinars, approved emails, iPad detailing) versus 45% in-person, a shift accelerated post-COVID and mirroring Pfizer's Comirnaty playbook.

Patient services via our OncoSupport hub drove 32% adherence improvement for OncoTarget-X, reducing 90-day discontinuation to 14% from 22% industry norm (per Symphony Health). DTC efforts, while nascent for our Rx-only portfolio, generated 1.2M impressions via unbranded NSCLC awareness campaigns on platforms like WebMD, yielding a 3.5x ROMI and 7% NRx lift in test DMAs.

Key Trends and Strategic Insights: YoY, we're seeing a 16% improvement in cost per NRx, down to $1,450 from $1,720, thanks to predictive analytics culling underperforming territories—we right-sized 5% of the force into high-ROI oncology pods. Biosimilar erosion remains a watch item; OncoTarget-X faces Janssen's biosimilar launch in '25, but our patent thicket and real-world evidence (RWE) from 15,000-patient ORION study bolsters defense, projecting <5% share loss.

Looking forward, we're allocating $180M to marketing in FY'25, with 40% to digital transformation—including a closed-loop marketing pilot with closed-loop attribution via our partnership with IQVIA's OneKey. This positions us to capture 2-3 share points in NSCLC amid the $50B IO market expansion, per Evaluate Pharma forecasts. Early reads on Q3 show NRx momentum at +20%, underscoring our edge in a payer-dominated landscape where 70% of US growth now ties to outcomes-based agreements.

Next, Karen Lee will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Karen Lee, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Tom. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. We've scaled viral vector production at our Singapore facility by 150% using single-use bioreactors for GeneXpert RA, and our new 50,000 L bioreactor in North Carolina targets 2x capacity by year-end for Pompe and Fabry readouts. Supply chain updates include partnerships with Lonza for continuous manufacturing and tech transfers reducing costs by 8% YoY. We are focused on biosecure resilience, with the Ireland fill-finish plant breaking ground soon to support EU launches and mitigate U.S. constraints.

Finally, Robert Singh will provide an update on regulatory submissions and approvals.

Robert Singh, Head of Regulatory Affairs:
Thank you, Karen. We continue to work closely with regulatory agencies. Good afternoon, everyone—before wrapping the prepared remarks, I want to highlight one of our most exciting areas of progress this quarter: regulatory approvals and label expansions. In the pharma and biotech space, these milestones are the lifeblood of value creation—they unlock new revenue streams, expand addressable markets, and solidify our competitive moats. We've had a banner quarter here, achieving three major approvals and two significant label expansions across our oncology, rare disease, and immunology portfolios.

First, our flagship oncology asset, Zorvix (zorviximab), our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibody that's been a cornerstone of our growth since its initial approval in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in 2022. This quarter, we secured FDA approval for a label expansion into small cell lung cancer (SCLC) in the first-line metastatic setting, based on the pivotal Phase 3 ZORVIX-SPRINT trial. This was a randomized, double-blind study versus investigator's choice chemotherapy, enrolling 682 patients across 140 sites globally. We hit all primary endpoints with statistical significance: progression-free survival (PFS) improved by 42%—median PFS of 9.2 months for Zorvix combo versus 6.4 months for chemo—hazard ratio of 0.58 (p<0.0001). Overall survival (OS) data were equally compelling, with a 28% reduction in risk of death (HR 0.72, p=0.002), and the safety profile remained consistent with prior data—Grade 3/4 TRAEs in just 22% of patients, comparable to Keytruda benchmarks.

This expansion is transformative. SCLC represents about 15% of lung cancers, a market underserved by immuno-oncology agents, where historical standards like etoposide-platinum have dismal 6-9 month PFS. Pre-approval, our NSCLC label captured a $4.2 billion U.S. TAM; adding SCLC boosts that by $1.1 billion annually, per IQVIA estimates. We project peak U.S. sales for Zorvix to exceed $2.8 billion by 2028, up from our prior $2.2 billion guide, driven by a 15-point share gain in first-line metastatic lung cancer—from our current 18% to 33%. Globally, we're filing with EMA by Q3 end, leveraging the trial's EU-heavy enrollment (35% of patients), and we've already initiated PMDA discussions in Japan, where lung cancer incidence is rising 4% YoY amid aging demographics.

Regionally, this positions us strongly in the U.S., where we'll launch immediately post-approval with our expanded sales force of 450 oncology specialists. In Europe, expect approval by mid-2025, tapping into the £800 million SCLC market fragmented by players like Roche's Tecentriq. Strategically, this de-risks our combo programs—think Zorvix plus our next-gen ADC, NovaLink-301, which just dosed its first patient in Phase 2—and supports our 20% CAGR oncology revenue target through 2030.

Moving to rare diseases, a huge win: full FDA approval of GenHeal (adeno-associated virus gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy Type 1, SMA1), following our BLA submission under priority review with Breakthrough Therapy Designation. This caps a whirlwind 10-month review—beating the PDUFA target by three weeks—based on the Phase 3 GENESIS trial in 48 infants. We achieved 92% event-free survival at 14 months versus 5% historical for supportive care, with sustained motor milestone gains mirroring Zolgensma's profile but with a differentiated IV administration slashing procedure costs by 40%. Pricing at $2.4 million per dose aligns with payers' willingness-to-pay, informed by our ICER dialogues.

GenHeal launches into a $3.5 billion global SMA market, where Novartis dominates with 85% share, but our one-time dosing and lower immunogenicity (anti-AAV9 titers <1:400 in 88% of patients) give us a durability edge. U.S. launch is underway, targeting 120-150 annual patients initially, with $350 million in Year 1 revenue potential ramping to $1.2 billion peak by 2029. Europe follows with EMA approval expected Q4 2024—our MAA is validated—and we've secured orphan incentives in China via NMPA fast-track, eyeing that $500 million Asia TAM where SMA newborn screening is expanding post-2023 mandates. This not only diversifies our revenue—rare diseases now 25% of total projected 2028 sales—but accelerates our gene therapy platform, with three more AAV candidates in Phase 2 for DMD and Pompe.

On label expansions, we notched two key ones. For ImmunoGuard (our IL-17 inhibitor akin to Cosentyx), FDA greenlit pediatric use in patients 6+ with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, off the back of the Phase 3 PEDS-IMMUNE trial (n=312). PASI-75 response was 84% at Week 16 versus 12% placebo, with no new safety signals. This expands our U.S. label from adults only, unlocking 450,000 pediatric patients—a 22% TAM uplift to $2.1 billion. Sales force deployment starts next month, and we're modeling $180 million incremental revenue in 2025, eroding AbbVie's Skyrizi share in this niche.

Finally, a technical expansion for Zorvix: FDA approval of a subcutaneous (SC) formulation via auto-injector, supported by PK/PD bridging studies showing bioequivalence to IV (AUC ratio 1.02, 90% CI 0.95-1.10). Patient preference trials (n=240) showed 91% electing SC for convenience, mirroring the Tremfya shift that boosted Janssen's compliance 35%. This cuts clinic time by 60%, boosting adherence in community settings, and we expect a 12% uptake within NSCLC by Year 2, adding $250 million to trough sales.

These achievements reflect broader industry tailwinds: FDA approvals hit a 10-year high in H1 2024 at 58 NDAs/BLAs, up 25% YoY, fueled by post-COVID manufacturing resilience and AI-accelerated trial design—like our SynthAI platform that slashed enrollment time 28% in ZORVIX-SPRINT. Competitively, we're outpacing peers; while Merck's Keytruda faces biosimilar headwinds post-2028 patent cliff, our bispecific moat and expansions position Zorvix for 15% market share in IO by 2030.

Strategically, this fuels our $15 billion 2028 revenue aspiration—45% from new indications—while de-risking the pipeline with 12 Phase 3 readouts by 2026. We've partnered with Lonza for 2x GenHeal capacity and inked a $1.2 billion deal with Samsung Biologics for fill-finish, ensuring supply chain robustness amid biosecure trends. M&A-wise, these milestones enhance our currency for bolt-ons, like the rumored $800 million rare disease tuck-in.

In summary, these regulatory wins add $2.5 billion to our NPV, with 60% U.S.-driven but accelerating ex-U.S. growth to 30% of sales by 2027. We're executing flawlessly in a high-barrier industry.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Emily.

Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:
Thank you, Robert. Before we move to Q&A, let me quickly touch on our business development activities, licensing deals, acquisitions, and partnerships, which continue to be a cornerstone of our strategy. In Q2, we executed three transformative deals—a licensing agreement, a tuck-in acquisition, and a strategic co-development partnership—that collectively added over $750 million in near-term cash inflows and more than $3.5 billion in potential milestone payments. Earlier this quarter, we in-licensed global rights—excluding Greater China—from SynthoBio for SBN-401, their Phase II-ready next-gen ADC targeting HER2-low breast cancer, paying $225 million upfront plus up to $1.8 billion in biobucks. We out-licensed ex-US rights to BNX-789, our Pompe gene therapy, to Chugai for $150 million upfront and $900 million milestones. On M&A, we closed a $450 million acquisition of AuraGenix, adding a T-cell engager and PROTAC degrader. Partnerships include expanding with Lonza for viral vectors and co-development with Broad Institute on siRNA for NASH. These enhance our 2025 revenue by $300-400 million and grow our pipeline to 18 programs.

On patent cliff exposure and life cycle management strategies, our top assets like Zyntra, HepaMax, and CardioVast face $5.1 billion at risk through 2028, with modeled 75-85% erosion. We've invested $1.2 billion in LCM, achieving 2.5-year extensions via label expansions (e.g., Zyntra in MSI-high), next-gen formulations like Zyntra SC, combos, litigation, and partnerships—preserving $800 million in 2024 revenues and offsetting cliffs for 12% growth through 2027.

Finally, cash flow and balance sheet highlights: We ended Q2 with $3.8 billion in cash, up $450 million sequentially, and net cash of $2.2 billion. Operating cash flow was $925 million in Q2, YTD $3.45 billion; free cash flow $810 million quarterly, $2.95 billion YTD. U.S. drove 78%, with efficiencies from inventory at 7.2 months and DSO at 52 days. This supports pipeline investments and $250 million repurchases.
